640	And to repent for this point, and then we merit that it be a vidui devarim before a talmid chacham.	E fazer teshuvá por esse ponto, e então merecemos que seja um vidui devarim diante de um talmid chacham.
641	Further on Rabbenu says: and then the Tzadik paves a path for the person according to the root of	Mais adiante Rabênu diz: e então o Tsadik abre para a pessoa um caminho segundo a raiz de
642	his soul.	sua alma.
643	We will see this later; it is one of the greatest gifts.
644	In this world, that a person merits that the Tzadik, from Heaven, in the merit,
645	by the power of the Tzadik, they pave a path for him according to the root of his soul.
646	What does it mean that they pave a path for him, in general, according to the root of his soul?
647	Every person comes into this world for a certain role, a certain tikun and a certain work.
648	Each one has his own particular level.
649	There is a saying of the Baal HaSulam, who writes in Sefer HaDaat: no person knows why he was sent
650	into his world.
651	Because we do not know this, since it is part of what HaShem hides from us, what
652	our exact role in the world is, they hide it, so many times we have questions about HaShem's
653	conduct.
654	Master of the world, why? I wanted to do something very good, and You prevented it from me, You did not let me do
655	anything good.
656	Why?
657	Many times they prevent it from Heaven: this is your role.
658	Not that you wanted something bad, you wanted something good, no problem, in Heaven they do not complain that you wanted the good thing,
659	you had good intention, so why did you not succeed?
660	Because it is not your role, very simply.
661	There is no point in your doing this, it is not your role.
662	Every person must do his own exact role.
663	And the Tzadik helps the person; what Rabbenu says, he paves a path for him according to
664	the root of his soul. The Tzadik helps the person go exactly according to the root of his soul, not to do things that are not...
665	even good things.
666	If it is not his tikun, then many times either to engage in it a little, or even not to engage in it
667	at all.
668	Why?
669	You did not come into the world for that.
670	There is a story about Rabbi Chaim Vital, he lived in Tzfat.
671	Even before the Holy Ari arrived, he lived in Tzfat.
672	And there were great giants there.
673	The great ones of the generations were there in Tzfat at that time: the Radbaz, the Shitah Mekubetzet, the Reshit Chochmah,
674	the Holy Shelah and more and more.
675	And he did not have, he did not feel the inclination of the heart to study Torah the way
676	they studied in that generation, the Gemara, in depth.
677	They were the great masters of in-depth study, the Radbaz, the Shitah Mekubetzet, all of them were very
678	great in-depth scholars.
